chunks: Permission is granted to those who fight because they were oppressed, and indeed, Allah is able to give help to them.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for fighting in self-defense against oppression?
ai.summary: This verse marks the transition from the Meccan period of passive endurance to the Medinan era of active defense, establishing the first legal permission (إذن) for fighting in Islam. In Shia exegesis, it is often linked to the concept of *jihād al-akbar* (greater jihad) of the self and *jihād al-asghar* (lesser jihad) of the sword, emphasizing that combat is a remedy for specific oppression rather than an end in itself. The affirmation of Allah's power (*laqadīr*) serves as a spiritual anchor for the believers, assuring divine support when they act justly against their aggressors.
